name: @remembrance-ai/mcp-server

tools.name: get_review_comparison
tools.description: Organization admin:review only. Read complete exact source, parent and current skill versions already linked to one pending review job. Supply no action, route, organization or arbitrary skill ID. This does not select a route or grant decision authority: inspect the current review detail and its fresh snapshot separately before any decision. An unavailable, held, changed or foreign reference refuses the whole comparison; nothing is truncated or silently substituted.

tools.name: repair_review_draft
tools.description: Organization admin:review only; explicit delegated AI review authority, not routine learning permission. Create one complete protected replacement for a pending private skill draft using its current unselected review snapshot. Use a stable psrr_ plus 32 lowercase hex request_id; the transport sets Idempotency-Key to that exact ID. Exact replay returns the original replacement receipt; changed input under that ID conflicts. All normal secret inspection, protection, routing, verification and review checks apply. The local client requires inspection to leave the authored capture unchanged before sending. A local hold returns content-free recovery, never an alternate transport or a rewritten original. Creation preserves the original and never approves, rejects or supersedes it. Review the replacement normally, then close the original separately only after proving an accepted, tenant-readable active replacement skill. No public or cross-organization fallback.

proposed_skill_md.description: Complete SKILL.md instructions: 80 to 56000 characters after trimming (UTF-16 code units). Capture refuses, before storing anything, a skill whose body is longer than that after local redaction, or whose delivery request as submitted or after redaction would exceed 262144 bytes of JSON. Nothing is truncated or split.

tools.name: get_connection_status
tools.description: Inspect the active Remembrance transport, credential source, authenticated registry scope, and content-free recent contribution outcomes for the current installation or API key without exposing credentials or lesson content. Call this before diagnosing authentication, checking environment variables, or making anonymous REST/browser probes. Local or bundled MCP can read REMEMBRANCE_API_KEY or ~/.config/remembrance/config.json; hosted MCP cannot read local files and authenticates from its request header. When a declared native lifecycle is degraded, local MCP may submit bounded, content-free health evidence unless REMEMBRANCE_HEALTH_REPORTING=0. Never infer the plugin's scope from REMEMBRANCE_API_KEY alone.

tools.name: run_connection_doctor
tools.description: Run a bounded, non-mutating Remembrance connection diagnostic. It verifies the active transport, a redacted registry destination, authenticated scope, query authorization, a real catalog read, and organization submission capability. Local MCP also checks shared-config permissions, destination consistency, native plugin lifecycle, and signing identity; hosted MCP marks local-only checks unavailable. It never submits content, creates query demand, opens a review item, or returns credentials, absolute paths, private registry URLs, prompts, or repository data.

active_read_probe.description: Verify a real authorized catalog read without creating query, feedback, or review records.

check_organization_write_authorization.description: Report organization submission authorization from the authenticated capability response without sending a write request.

tools.name: query_skills
tools.description: Call before non-trivial service, API, tool, library, workflow, UI, review, test, security, or deployment work to find relevant Remembrance skills and resources. This is a read-only routine action: do not ask the user for a separate conversational permission step. For short context-dependent follow-ups, infer the concrete task from the full conversation, preserve any plugin-supplied client_context.directive_id/runtime/trigger_reason, and query anyway. Compare each candidate's bounded why_matched evidence and applicability conditions before opening it; discard stated unlikely or corner-case mismatches. High matches should be fetched before custom work; possible and exploratory matches remain optional. Do not use for broad web search or one-off facts. Results refer by key or preference_fingerprint to preferences stated once in top-level effective_preferences, and get_skill returns the full text of a description_truncated summary. semantic_status says, without content, whether vector retrieval contributed to each result list; lexical_only results remain usable.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: Browse the live authorized skill catalog without loading full instructions. q is an indexed normalized slug-prefix filter for resolving an explicit name or partial slug; it is not relevance search. Use query_skills for discovery, and never guess the exact slug passed to invoke_skill. Organization results include eligible private skills and allowed public skills, with private same-slug skills taking precedence.

tools.name: invoke_skill
tools.description: Load an explicitly selected skill through the authoritative policy boundary. Use an exact slug returned by list_skills, an MCP resource, or query_skills. This resolves the current active reviewed version, records direct selection, and returns post-use feedback and outcome instructions. Pass version_id only when a session-start directive or subagent handoff supplies one; that exact version is loaded and never substituted, and 409 skill_version_unavailable means it cannot be served. Use scope session only for an organization session skill named by a session-start directive; omit scope for ordinary task use. Do not use submit_query_feedback for this explicit selection.

version_id.description: Exact reviewed version to load, only when a session-start directive or subagent handoff supplies one. The current or a superseded version is served; another version is never substituted, and an unavailable one returns 409 skill_version_unavailable.

scope.description: session only for an organization session skill named by a session-start directive: reloading the same skill version with the same idempotency_key returns the first invocation. Omit for ordinary task use.

tools.name: get_effective_preferences
tools.description: Return bounded, task-relevant working preferences for this verified installation and optional linked member/runtime profile. project_key is an opaque local project-context hash; paths and repository names are never transmitted. A clear current-task preference overrides every non-mandatory stored preference; Required organization guidance remains authoritative. Preferences may steer among already-relevant skills and surgically alter discretionary presentation, workflow, or strategy choices. They never change relevance tiers or weaken applicability, safety, authorization, privacy, required skill steps, validation, or review. Clients without a valid principal session remain organization-level and receive no personal preferences. The response's personalization block says which stored-preference scopes were actually read: available true means every scope applying to this caller was read, so an empty effective_preferences list is a real empty profile, and resolved_scopes names them. available false names what was not read: organization_scope_only (no principal session, so the installation, member and runtime scopes in omitted_scopes were never queried and a stored personal preference may simply not be listed), not_applicable (anonymous, so no organization-scoped storage applies), preference_storage_unavailable, or preferences_disabled. Discovery and invocation stay available in every case, and none of these states requires authentication or adds a prompt. Follow the part of a preference written for this host. Unlike an outage, one naming a model, tool, or agent this host lacks, with no part for this host, was written for another agent family: apply the closest equivalent this host supports and say which. When none is safe to assume, ask the user; if you cannot ask, keep your default and say so.

tools.name: get_private_lesson_policy
tools.description: Fetch and cryptographically verify the authenticated organization's signed private-lesson automation policy. The server response never exposes an organization id and public_fallback is always false. The local MCP augments this with secure outbox readiness; hosted-only clients report auto_capture_supported=false.

supported_max_payload_bytes.description: Largest canonical private-lesson payload, in UTF-8 bytes, that this client can submit. The server signs the largest limit it supports up to this value; without it, the policy names the legacy 4096-byte limit.

tools.name: record_preference
tools.description: Record a bounded, privacy-safe preference observation for the current verified installation. Built-in settings need only key and value; a custom setting also supplies its plain-language label, behavior, presentation/workflow/strategy_selection effect, prefer/avoid direction, and definition version. Send normalized settings and hashes only, never prompt text. A valid principal session is required. An explicit instruction governs the current task immediately. This call does not guarantee activation: read activated and normalized_activation_state in the response rather than assuming the setting is live. Known built-ins normally activate durably at once, custom settings remain pending until automatic normalization and validation approves them, and inferred observations activate only after Remembrance's consistency and confidence thresholds are met. Organizations on customer-held encryption are deferred: every substantive preference write is refused before persistence with HTTP 422 and code customer_held_preference_processing_deferred, existing records are unchanged, and reads plus the content-free withdrawal lane keep working. Do not retry that refusal, and do not offer preference compatibility feedback there. To keep an adaptation of another agent family's preference, record it for this runtime only: scope member_runtime, the same key, and a value, label, and behavior naming your equivalent; use source_category explicit_user only when the user confirmed it. Never overwrite the original in a shared installation or member scope. If member_runtime is refused because this installation is not linked to a member, keep the adaptation to this task and say once that linking the installation lets it persist.

tools.name: submit_preference_compatibility_feedback
tools.description: After actually opening or invoking a skill, record whether that exact version supports or conflicts with one server-issued active working-preference fingerprint. An unavailable host tool or model is not by itself a skill conflict; runtime capability is a separate question. This is private to the authenticated organization, requires the same verified installation principal that used the correlated query/result, and never changes the skill or another organization's ranking. Use evidence_source explicit_user only for a user's explicit assessment; otherwise use agent_observed. Send only correlation IDs, the returned fingerprint, exact slug/version id, relationship, source, and an optional allowlisted reason_code; never send prompts, source code, paths, free-text feedback, or a caller-generated idempotency hash. Organizations on customer-held encryption are deferred: the server withholds the preference_compatibility_feedback offer there and refuses this call before persistence with HTTP 422 and code customer_held_preference_processing_deferred. Call it only when a response actually offered the fingerprint, and never retry that refusal.

tools.name: link_current_installation
tools.description: Link this verified installation to the signed-in organization member using a single-use dashboard token. The token expires after ten minutes and is consumed exactly once. A valid organization principal session is required; this never changes the organization API key or creates another billed agent.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Fetch the exact active reviewed skill body and version after query_skills returns a known slug. The response includes skill_md, version_id, and source. Pass query_id and result_id from that response so Remembrance can measure whether surfaced guidance was opened. Do not guess private or inactive slugs.

query_id.description: Originating query_id, when this result came from query_skills.

tools.name: get_resource
tools.description: Fetch a known resource by slug after query_skills returns it. Pass query_id and result_id from that response so Remembrance can measure whether surfaced guidance was opened. Do not use for arbitrary URL fetching.

query_id.description: Originating query_id, when this result came from query_skills.

tools.name: bootstrap_agent_identity
tools.description: Create or reuse a local Ed25519 TOFU key and register it with Remembrance. No arguments are required. Rerun to repair permissions or re-bootstrap if the local agent-key.json was lost.

subject.description: Optional stable agent identity. Omit it to generate a private opaque subject from the new public-key fingerprint.

provider.description: Use other for independent TOFU keys. Use codex/cursor/claude_code only for Remembrance-registered plugin keys.

key_path.description: Override key file path. Defaults to XDG config.

force_rotate.description: Generate and register a new key even when one exists.

tools.name: acknowledge_feedback_denial
tools.description: Acknowledge one exact submit_query_feedback or submit_feedback event that the host denied before transport. This writes only a private, content-free, hashed local marker with 14-day retention. It performs no network request, grants no approval, retries nothing, and never records feedback payload or draft content. Use result_id only for submit_feedback.

tools.name: decline_pending_action
tools.description: Decline one pending Remembrance action that a hook reminder listed and you cannot complete. Pass the action_id shown under it and one reason: not_observed_by_this_agent (you never received the result or payload it refers to), agent_exited (the subagent that earned it has exited), not_reusable (it holds nothing reusable), or duplicate (it was already completed another way); host_policy_denied only for a private-learning line or notice whose exact action the host denied. It is local-only: it sends nothing, stores nothing, grants no approval, and never counts as feedback. The local completion hook closes that action in your own pending list when it observes this call; a declined private draft stays retained and returns later only as a user decision.

action_id.description: The action_id shown under the pending action in the hook reminder.

reason.description: Why this agent cannot complete the action.

tools.name: get_pending_action_payload
tools.description: Return the exact payload a pending Remembrance action keeps on this machine, when a hook reminder names it with an action_id and a ledger instead of showing it. Pass both as shown. It reads only that ledger, verifies the payload against its recorded digest, and returns it unchanged with its kind and provenance: a reusable-evidence follow-up's submit_remembrance payload as payload, or a durable preference's exact record_preference arguments as arguments. Provenance is first_hand; second_hand when an exited subagent left it; subagent_identity_unavailable or pre_agent_keying when the record cannot say which agent earned it. It is local-only: it sends nothing, submits or records nothing, applies no preference, and changes nothing. A kept payload stays until its action is completed, declined or withdrawn. A payload that was never kept, or cannot be opened or verified, is reported as such and never guessed; then use only a payload or arguments you still hold verbatim, or decline the action. A missing key is recovered only by restoring the original key; a new key cannot open it.

action_id.description: The action_id the hook demand names for the payload.

ledger.description: The ledger the hook demand names with that action_id.

tools.name: capture_learning
tools.description: The zero-network routine reusable-learning entry point for a capture-capable local client; use it silently without a separate conversational permission step. Supply exactly one compact lesson, complete private skill, or structured preference observation. The local router chooses the organization-private lane, encrypts lesson and skill drafts before persistence, and returns one exact next action. The preference route persists nothing locally (persisted_locally false); record_preference completes it, so read that response rather than assuming the preference is live. Call that action immediately; the host asks for approval only when the private network lane is not already approved. Complete skills receive a persisted trusted inspector digest and exactly one outcome: unchanged, redacted (source-redacted), positive_recovery_need, or operational_failure. Only a positive recovery need for confirmed source-ownership ambiguity or a recognized encrypted private container returns agent_recovery. Capacity, internal, and inspector-contract faults are operational failures, never semantic ambiguity or permission to reformulate. A replacement_of submission must be a fresh complete skill, preserve adequate task meaning, and pass full inspection; recovery context is separately inspected, explicitly partial, and never the unchecked held original. Each inspector/context epoch accepts at most three distinct candidate digests; only a new authenticated native-user session context or trusted inspector identity opens another. The original and attempts remain encrypted until private acceptance, which completes the draft through the existing private_skill approval lane without another approval. If adequate context is unavailable, retain the draft; do not invent instructions or ask the user to inspect files. It never accepts organization, destination, visibility, credential, or public-fallback fields. Query-result fit is intentionally excluded: always use submit_query_feedback for good, partial, or poor query matches.

capture_id.description: Optional opaque lesson capture identity: cap_ followed by 32 random lowercase hexadecimal characters. Allocate before the first lesson call and reuse with the identical lesson after a lost response. Inspect it locally to reconcile first. A different lesson or destination is refused for the same identity. Supported only with lesson; it grants no submission approval.

generalized_lesson.description: One compact, generalized lesson. Limit: 1200 characters, measured after local redaction, not on the raw text. Redaction replaces secrets, paths, URLs, and similar values with markers such as [redacted:public_url], which can make the text shorter or longer. A longer lesson is refused and nothing is stored. A complete reusable procedure belongs in the private-skill lane instead: capture_learning with private_skill, or propose_private_skill (up to 56000 characters).

stable_conditions.description: Up to 12 conditions under which the lesson holds. Limit: 240 characters per condition, measured after local redaction; redaction markers can make a condition shorter or longer. A longer condition is refused and nothing is stored. A complete reusable procedure belongs in the private-skill lane instead: capture_learning with private_skill, or propose_private_skill (up to 56000 characters).

proposed_skill_md.description: Complete SKILL.md instructions: 80 to 56000 characters after trimming (UTF-16 code units). Capture refuses, before storing anything, a skill whose body is longer than that after local redaction, or whose delivery request as submitted or after redaction would exceed 262144 bytes of JSON. Nothing is truncated or split.

draft_id.description: Retained encrypted private-skill draft being replaced.

context_source.description: Audit-only source label: active_task_context or separately inspected, explicitly partial safe_recovery_context. Neither source is submission authority.

recovery_context_id.description: Omit this field unless the current inspect_private_learning_outbox agent_recovery.arguments.replacement_of supplies this exact ID. Never invent an ID or derive one from a draft, digest, or ordinary recovery_context. A supplied native context ID may establish a new context epoch but grants no approval or authority to reuse held content. safe_recovery_context alone does not require an ID.

draft_id.description: Held private-lesson draft that this lesson replaces, from its agent_recovery. Write the lesson from the current task, without what the findings name; the held content is never available. The held draft is retired only once the organization accepts this lesson, and accepts at most three versions; a held version is refused with its findings.

replacement_of.description: Optional lineage for a replacement of one retained draft: a complete private skill for a private-skill draft, or a lesson for a held private-lesson draft. It carries audit/context identity only and grants no approval, destination authority, or permission to reuse held content.

tools.name: inspect_private_learning_outbox
tools.description: Inspect local state for both encrypted private-learning outboxes without a network request. Listings contain per-lane status, draft IDs, retry metadata, retained bytes, trusted persisted inspector outcomes/digests, and recovery reason codes without original candidate payloads or paths. Set private_skill_draft_id to inspect one exact draft independently of pagination. The four skill outcomes are unchanged, redacted (source-redacted), positive_recovery_need, and operational_failure. Only positive recovery need can expose separately inspected, explicitly partial native context and agent_recovery; capacity and other inspection faults remain operational. The held original is never returned as context. Recovery uses at most three distinct candidate digests per inspector/context epoch. Candidate text, duplicates, and timers do not reset the bound; only new authenticated native-user session context or trusted inspector identity can open another epoch. Follow eligible recovery autonomously through the existing private_skill approval lane. Unavailable context and operational failures remain encrypted for a later valid lifecycle opportunity, not submitted or discarded; do not invent instructions or ask the user to inspect files. One corrupt lane cannot hide the other.

private_skill_draft_id.description: Inspect this exact retained skill regardless of listing order. A positive recovery need may return separately inspected, explicitly partial native context; operational failures, including capacity faults, do not. This never returns the held original, submits content, or grants approval.

tools.name: queue_private_skill_import
tools.description: Local-only fallback for an organization-approved skill contribution that a host privacy or network policy would not send. Writes a mode-0600 organization-private handoff bundle without contacting Remembrance. It never submits or syncs the content: an organization admin must deliberately upload the file through Dashboard > Skills > Import, where every skill enters the normal private review flow. Do not use another transport to evade a host denial and do not claim the skills were submitted.

tools.name: prepare_private_lesson_candidate
tools.description: Locally canonicalize, redact, validate, encrypt, and durably queue one compact organization-private failure, correction, or evidence lesson. Limits apply after local redaction: generalized_lesson at most 1200 characters and each stable_conditions item at most 240; an over-limit call is refused with the field and its length, and nothing is stored. This is an evidence lane, not a complete-skill transport: use propose_private_skill or propose_skill_idea for a complete reusable procedure, playbook, or actionable instructions. Tags use an open, bounded lowercase slug vocabulary; a malformed or privacy-sensitive tag is dropped and counted. Every redaction match becomes its [redacted:category] marker and the draft continues; only a stack trace or zero-width or bidirectional control characters hold it as held_safety. Pre-redaction input remains memory-only and this tool performs no network request. The result returns a draft handle and never echoes lesson prose. Follow the returned next_action with submit_private_lesson_candidate; held_safety content remains local. An unsupported redactor version or digest becomes terminal superseded_redactor and is never retried or re-redacted.

generalized_lesson.description: One compact, generalized lesson. Limit: 1200 characters, measured after local redaction, not on the raw text. Redaction replaces secrets, paths, URLs, and similar values with markers such as [redacted:public_url], which can make the text shorter or longer. A longer lesson is refused and nothing is stored. A complete reusable procedure belongs in the private-skill lane instead: capture_learning with private_skill, or propose_private_skill (up to 56000 characters).

tools.name: inspect_private_lesson_outbox
tools.description: Inspect content-free state, retained bytes, terminal reasons, deletion guidance, retry metadata, and one reachable page of encrypted local private-lesson drafts. Use offset with next_offset until truncated is false; selecting draft_id remains independent of pagination. This never returns lesson prose or canonical payload bytes. Terminal drafts remain retained and count toward the safety ceiling until explicitly deleted.

capture_id.description: Reconcile one lesson capture by its opaque capture_id without replaying lesson content. Omit draft_id when selecting capture_id.

offset.description: Zero-based local page offset. Follow next_offset until truncated is false.

tools.name: submit_private_lesson_candidate
tools.description: Submit exactly one canonical, challenge-attested organization-private lesson candidate or one content-free held-safety telemetry event. Local plugin clients normally pass only the draft_id returned by capture_learning; raw or hosted clients pass the strict candidate-or-hold union. The action always creates only an organization-private submission and never falls back to anonymous or public submission. Held telemetry contains no lesson prose and can never enter verification, review, topology, or skill materialization. Exact replay is idempotent; host denial leaves the local draft untouched.

draft_id.description: Local private-lesson draft returned by capture_learning.
Local private-lesson draft returned by capture_learning.

tools.name: retry_private_lesson_candidate
tools.description: Retry one retained private-lesson draft through the same private_lesson approval lane as submit_private_lesson_candidate. Network access is allowed only for authorization-pending, due transient retry, newly compatible profile, or refreshable policy states, and for a held draft the current local safety check releases once the user chose to deliver it (deliver_rechecked_hold=true); a fresh ready draft is rejected locally. A legacy_destination_recovery review explicitly requests a content-free signed-policy review for one eligible unbound draft, without changing or sending it. Only new explicit owner approval of that exact review and all outbox readers at 0.2.6 or newer permits local destination binding; a separate normal retry performs delivery. Never infer migration approval from submission approval. It never falls back to a public or alternate transport.

draft_id.description: Local private-lesson draft returned by capture_learning.

deliver_rechecked_hold.description: Only after the user chose to deliver a held draft whose safety_recheck is passes_current_rule: send it under the current safety rule. A draft the current check still holds is refused locally and not sent.

legacy_destination_recovery.description: Explicit legacy destination recovery only. review requests a content-free plan using the signed current organization policy; it changes no draft and sends no lesson. approve requires the exact review fields, new explicit owner confirmation that this draft belongs only to that organization and may be delivered there, the SHA-256 hash of that approval, and confirmation every outbox reader is Remembrance 0.2.6 or newer. Existing submission approval is not migration approval. Approval binds the unchanged encrypted draft locally and returns its normal retry; it does not submit it. Never infer the old destination, reveal retained source, or approve on the owner's behalf.

tools.name: delete_private_lesson_candidate
tools.description: Explicitly delete one selected local private-lesson draft. confirm=true is required. No automatic cleanup exists, and deletion leaves only a content-free tombstone.

draft_id.description: Local private-lesson draft returned by capture_learning.

confirm.description: Must be true. Deletion is explicit and leaves a content-free tombstone.

tools.name: submit_private_skill_candidate
tools.description: Submit exactly one encrypted local complete-skill draft to the authenticated organization's private review and verification pipeline. Pass only the draft_id returned by capture_learning. The action never accepts a visibility or organization override and never falls back to public submission. An idempotent private acceptance completes the selected original or replacement and removes the encrypted original, recovery contexts, and attempt content; recovery reuses this existing private_skill approval lane rather than requesting another approval.

draft_id.description: Encrypted local private-skill draft returned by capture_learning.

tools.name: retry_private_skill_candidate
tools.description: Retry one retained private-skill draft through the same private_skill approval lane as submit_private_skill_candidate. Network access is allowed only for authorization-pending or due transient retry states, an explicit same-draft retry after an administrator corrected a private-protection configuration hold, and for a draft an older server refused only for length: that waits out any delay the server set, then reads its signed capability and resends the exact draft only if it admits it. Configuration holds never schedule automatic retries; an unchanged refusal remains held. A fresh ready draft is rejected locally. It never switches transport, visibility, key ownership, or protection mode.

draft_id.description: Encrypted local private-skill draft returned by capture_learning.

tools.name: delete_private_skill_candidate
tools.description: Explicitly delete one selected local private-skill draft. confirm=true is required. Unsubmitted drafts are never removed automatically; successful content is removed immediately and its content-free completion marker expires after 14 days.

draft_id.description: Encrypted local private-skill draft returned by capture_learning.

confirm.description: Must be true. Deletion is explicit and leaves only a content-free tombstone.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Submit categorical post-use skill feedback without a separate conversational permission request: useful or not useful, an optional rating, and the originating query_id/result_id when the skill came from query_skills. Reusable prose is deliberately not accepted here; call capture_learning separately for a generalized lesson, complete private skill, or preference. This tool never replaces submit_query_feedback, which remains the only query-fit verdict path.

verified_attestation.description: When true, sign the feedback with the local TOFU key. Missing local identity is initialized automatically; bootstrap_agent_identity remains available for preflight or recovery.

tools.name: submit_query_feedback
tools.description: Submit one complete set of bounded explicit good, partial, or poor judgments for result_id values from one query_skills call, using the same auth scope as that query. Use overall_fit none only when every rated result is poor; if any result is partial or good, use partial or good as appropriate. Keep honest per-result judgments when correcting validation errors; do not drop them or relabel matches to bypass validation. Each result_id appears once; poor ratings require at least one reason. This bounded feedback action carries no reusable content and needs no separate conversational permission request. Unrated results stay neutral. Notes are optional and compact; this path remains independent of private learning capture and never accepts a reusable lesson. Keep routine organization ratings minimal: use the Remembrance-issued query_id and result_id values, judgments, required reasons, and an idempotency key when needed, and do not automatically attach internal artifact hashes, task text, source snippets, or raw logs. An identical retry is safe, but changed later judgments conflict. Labels adjust bounded retrieval profiles without changing global skill usefulness; use submit_feedback only after actually using a skill.

overall_fit.description: Use none only when every rated result is poor. If any result is partial or good, use partial or good as appropriate; preserve honest per-result judgments.

reasons.description: At least one reason is required when fit is poor.

results.description: One verdict per result_id. Required and nonempty for overall_fit good or partial. With overall_fit none, every supplied verdict must be poor. Do not discard judgments to bypass validation.

poor_result_requires_reason.message: Poor matches require at least one reason.
poor_result_requires_reason.remediation: Keep the result verdict and supply at least one published reason for each poor match.

rated_results_required.message: A good or partial overall fit requires at least one result verdict.
rated_results_required.remediation: Include the known result verdicts. Use overall_fit none only when no result fits.

duplicate_result_id.message: Each result_id may appear only once.
duplicate_result_id.remediation: Combine duplicate entries into one honest verdict per result_id; keep the other judgments.

overall_none_requires_poor_results.message: When overall_fit is none, every rated result must be marked poor.
overall_none_requires_poor_results.remediation: If any result is partial or good, use overall_fit partial or good as appropriate. Preserve honest per-result ratings; do not drop the results array or relabel matches to bypass validation.

tools.name: report_task_outcome
tools.description: Report completion or abandonment for a query. Remembrance accepts one terminal outcome per query; retry the same report with the same idempotency_key, and do not submit a different later outcome. Include only result_ids listed in task_outcome.eligible_result_ids; each result and bundle also carries task_outcome_eligible. When two or three selected skills exactly match a returned skill_bundles entry, include its bundle_id for value attribution; other combinations are accepted as funnel telemetry but do not train a skill or bundle cohort. Include bounded token totals only when the runtime exposes them. For Vercel AI Gateway work, include metering_reference.adapter=vercel_ai_gateway and every gen_ generation ID used by the task (maximum eight); Remembrance retrieves authoritative usage asynchronously, and caller totals never establish proof trust. Never send prompts, outputs, source paths, private URLs, transcripts, or proprietary task content. Completion without token counts still closes the funnel but cannot establish metered savings proof.

tools.name: get_value_proof
tools.description: Fetch and cryptographically verify the token-only signed proof referenced by a qualified potential_savings estimate. Successful results include signature_verified=true. Public-skill proofs are anonymous reads; organization-skill proofs require an active query-capable API key from the same organization, but not necessarily the key used for the original query. Proof payloads contain no organization identity, task identity, price, credit, subscription, or payment data.

id.description: Value proof id returned with potential_savings.

tools.name: submit_remembrance
tools.description: Submit a full remembrance payload with detailed reusable evidence, including high-value self-corrections, user-caught mistakes, CI/deploy failures, and release/versioning misses as type failure_report. Never include credentials, secrets, raw logs, or unrelated repository content. Repository-derived private instructions may be sent only when the user or organization has approved Remembrance as a destination. If the host blocks that export, report that nothing was sent and do not retry through another transport or create a handoff unless an organization admin explicitly requests one.

tools.name: propose_skill_idea

This full skill lane retains bounded markdown, public citations, snippets, metadata, and actionable instructions through normal safety and review; do not compress a finished skill into the narrow private-lesson contract. THIS TOOL'S VISIBILITY IS NOT FIXED: an active organization API key keeps the candidate inside that organization's review queue, while intentionally calling without a key creates a PUBLIC candidate. A supplied invalid/inactive key fails with 401 and a valid key without submission:create fails with 403; neither failure creates a candidate. Prefer propose_private_skill for anything repository-derived, organization-specific, or otherwise not intended for the public registry because that endpoint structurally requires organization auth. Use propose_skill_idea only when a public candidate is an acceptable outcome. Check `visibility` (organization_private or public_candidate) and `owner_scope` in the successful response, and report where the candidate landed. Never remove or bypass an organization key to force public submission: submit privately, then use the reviewed public-propagation flow. A 422 skill_routing_metadata_incomplete stores nothing and carries the same draft.

tools.name: propose_private_skill

Prefer it whenever the content is repository-derived, organization-specific, or must not reach the public registry; that preference is about removing the credential from the privacy decision, not about propose_skill_idea being unsafe when a key is present. instructions:
Remembrance is shared operational memory for agents. Core rules (details follow; some hosts show only this part):
- Before non-trivial service, API, tool, library, workflow, UI, review, test, security, or deployment work, including short follow-ups, call query_skills for the task inferred from the conversation. Open a high match with get_skill or get_resource, passing query_id and result_id; discard poor fits.
- Honor skill_access: when org_only, use only returned organization skills; fail closed when the policy cannot be confirmed.
- After query_skills, rate the results once with submit_query_feedback. After actually using a result, call submit_feedback and follow its outcome instructions.
- Submit reusable lessons with submit_remembrance and new workflows with propose_private_skill; never bypass an organization key to publish. Host-local memory does not replace this.
- For a named skill, resolve it with list_skills and call invoke_skill with an exact returned slug; never guess.
- Preferences steer only discretionary choices; required organization settings always apply. Follow the part of a preference written for this host. Unlike an outage, one naming a model, tool, or agent this host lacks, with no part for this host, was written for another agent family: apply the closest equivalent this host supports and say which. When none is safe to assume, ask the user; if you cannot ask, keep your default and say so. Keep an adaptation only with record_preference scope member_runtime.
- Call run_connection_doctor before claiming Remembrance is unconfigured or anonymous. Never print or request the raw key.
- Send summaries and hashes, never secrets, credentials, private URLs, raw logs, or proprietary content.
- If the host blocks a Remembrance action, report it once as not submitted and do not retry it another way.
- Before finishing, self-check for a missed query and submit a failure_report remembrance for a caught mistake or failure.

Details:
Before claiming that Remembrance is anonymous, unconfigured, partially active, or missing an organization key, call run_connection_doctor for the transport you will actually use. It performs a safe catalog read and returns exact bounded remediation without submitting content. Use get_connection_status only when you need the underlying transport and lifecycle fields. An unset REMEMBRANCE_API_KEY does not prove that a local plugin is anonymous because local hooks and bundled MCP may read ~/.config/remembrance/config.json. Conversely, hosted MCP cannot read that local file. Anonymous curl or browser probes describe only those requests, not plugin authentication. Never print or request the raw key. When the user explicitly names an authorized Remembrance skill or supplies a remembrance://skills/{slug} URI, resolve ambiguous names with list_skills using its normalized slug-prefix filter, then call invoke_skill with an exact returned slug. Never guess a slug. list_skills is catalog resolution, not relevance search; use query_skills when the user wants relevant candidates rather than a known selection. invoke_skill rechecks authorization and organization policy, resolves the current reviewed version, and returns the only full instruction body. Catalog listings and MCP resource reads are lightweight handles, not skill use. Do not run query_skills merely to rediscover that explicit selection, and do not submit query-fit feedback for it. After meaningful direct use, follow the returned task-outcome and post-use feedback instructions once. BEFORE non-trivial service/API/tool/library/workflow/UI/review/test/security/deployment work, call query_skills to reuse proven skills and resources instead of rediscovering them. A local repository change still qualifies when it involves a reusable workflow or lesson; skip only genuinely trivial throwaway edits and one-off facts. For short follow-ups such as 'fix these issues', 'continue', or 'try again', infer the concrete task, domain, and constraints from the full conversation and still call query_skills; do not wait for the current prompt to repeat trigger keywords. Treat match_tier as a decision aid, then inspect why_matched and applicability before opening a result. These fields show bounded matched terms/capabilities, constraint text overlap, qualitative lexical/semantic evidence, declared scope, use conditions, and exclusions without exposing unstable raw ranking scores. satisfied_constraints and missed_constraints describe textual overlap only, not verified compliance or proven capability gaps. Discard an unlikely or irrelevant corner-case result and report fit: poor; do not force its use. For a remaining high match, call get_skill or get_resource before custom work and pass the returned query_id/result_id so the surfaced-to-fetch funnel closes; possible and exploratory matches are optional. The response also includes approximate context tokens, verified uses, risk, tags, permissions, dependencies, and contraindications so you can weigh the detour safely. Honor query_skills.skill_access on every response. When policy is org_only, use only returned organization skills and never substitute bundled or live public skill references; if an organization key is configured and the query is unavailable, fail closed because the policy cannot be confirmed. AFTER query_skills, call submit_query_feedback once with one complete set of explicit good/partial/poor judgments using the returned query_id and result_id values; leave unrated results neutral, and remember that a poor query match is not the same as a globally bad skill. Reuse the same organization or anonymous auth scope as the query. AFTER you actually use a skill or resource, close the post-use loop with submit_feedback (useful true/false plus a one-line lesson and the originating query_id/result_id; it returns a ready submit_remembrance payload), then submit_remembrance if the lesson is reusable. If nothing fit and you built a new workflow, use propose_private_skill for an organization-private candidate. With an organization key, propose_skill_idea also remains organization-private. Never remove, suppress, or bypass that key to force a public submission; submit privately, then use the reviewed public-propagation flow when the organization chooses to share it. When delegating, pass the selected slug, exact version, query_id, and result_id to the subagent; it should invoke/fetch that result or run its own full-context query. The parent reports the terminal outcome unless the subagent creates its own invocation. Route memory deliberately: host-local memory is for facts about this human, repository, or machine; Remembrance is for generalized lessons another approved organization agent would otherwise rediscover. A local-memory write does not satisfy organization-shared capture. Before finishing any reusable task, self-check for a missed query. If you catch your own mistake, the user catches one, CI/deploy fails, a security issue appears, or you fix a release/versioning miss, submit a failure_report remembrance even if no skill was used; raw MCP clients have no plugin Stop hook to remind you later. After an observed host-policy denial, report only the affected action once: 'The host blocked this Remembrance action. Do not treat it as submitted. Earlier successful actions are unaffected; querying remains available.' Do not retry the blocked content through another transport or claim submission. If submit_query_feedback or submit_feedback was denied before transport and acknowledge_feedback_denial is available, call that local-only tool with the exact tool, query_id, result_id only for submit_feedback, and reason host_policy_denied. It suppresses that blocked reminder without claiming feedback was submitted, changing approvals, or blocking future feedback. When host events are unavailable, use this explicit acknowledgment; do not infer denial from API errors. Do not repeat warnings already reported. Attach evidence (reproduction detail, artifact hashes, or an attestation); evidence-less public reports wait in unverified intake until corroborated. Redact secrets, private URLs, credentials, raw logs, and proprietary content; submit summaries and hashes, not raw traces. Keep routine organization query-fit and categorical post-use ratings minimal: use the Remembrance-issued query_id/result_id values, judgments, required reasons, and an idempotency key when needed. Do not automatically attach internal artifact hashes, task text, source snippets, or raw logs to routine ratings. Optional evidence is not required for these ratings; public substantive reports still need evidence. Standing approval for these two feedback tools does not authorize reusable content submission or override host policy, organization scope, or processing consent.
